## What's Changed
* perf: reduce history restore allocations and interrupted recovery hydration by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/394
* docs: add extension contribution link to README by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/395
* fix(rpc): correlate and settle every native execution lease by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/396
* feat(extensions): follow the catalog move to pi-rust/rpi-extension by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/398
* feat(tui): support explicit hiding in entry renderers by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/399
* fix(harness): follow context symlinks and shadow nested worktrees by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/403
* ci: stop reporting a monitor 403 as channel drift by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/404
* docs: refresh WeChat group image cache key by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/402
* chore(release): prepare 0.27.1 by @bigfish1913 in https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/pull/401


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/compare/v0.27.0...v0.27.1

# rpi — a Rust-native coding-agent runtime

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/crates/d/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli) [![license](https://img.shields.io/crates/l/rpi-cli.svg)](#license) [![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/MSRV-1.88-blue.svg)](#install) [![CI](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bigfish1913/pi-rust?style=flat)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/stargazers) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/bigfish1913/pi-rust)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/releases/latest) [![Best of Agent Harnesses](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%8F%86_Best_of-Agent_Harnesses-5ac4bf)](https://github.com/RyanAlberts/best-of-Agent-Harnesses) `rpi` is a library-first coding-agent runtime written in Rust, plus a terminal agent built on top of it. Eleven composable crates span provider adapters, a durable crash-resumable agent loop, a reusable runtime, a terminal UI, and a stable plugin ABI — so the same code works as an embedded SDK or as a ready-to-run `rpi` command. rpi began as a Rust reimplementation of the [Pi TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) by Mario Zechner. It now includes its own Rust-native plugin ABI and execution infrastructure. See [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) and [NOTICE](NOTICE) for upstream attribution. [Website](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/) · [Docs](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/docs.html) · [Extension catalog](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html) · [Submit an extension](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/submit.html) · [rpi-extension](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension) ## See it in action ![rpi interactive session](docs/images/rpi-interactive.png) Interactive TUI, recorded with an isolated configuration. See the [user guide](docs/guides/user-guide.md) for the full command surface. ![rpi terminal demo — opening the built-in help without a model request](docs/images/rpi-tui-demo.gif) Open the terminal agent and explore `/help`, with no real API key or model request. Recording script: [`demo/tui.tape`](demo/tui.tape). ![rpi SDK demo — an agent loop and a real tool round-trip, offline with the faux provider](docs/images/rpi-sdk-demo.gif) The agent loop and a real `write` tool round-trip, recorded with no API key and no network — the same path the tests take. Source of truth is [`demo/sdk.tape`](demo/sdk.tape); regenerate with `task demo`. ## Three ways to use it | You want | Depend on | Start at | | -------- | --------- | -------- | | A working terminal coding agent | nothing | `cargo install rpi-cli` | | Your own agent inside your process | `rpi-agent` (+ `rpi-ai`, `rpi-tools`) | [`examples/minimal`](examples/minimal) | | A tool/provider that extends every session | `rpi-plugin-sdk` | [`examples/plugin-stub`](examples/plugin-stub) | The three share one implementation. Build your tools once, debug them inside an embedded agent, and ship the same code as a `cdylib` plugin that the global `rpi` loads. See [`docs/agent/project-structure.md`](docs/agent/project-structure.md) for the recommended project layout. ## Install **Prebuilt binary** (no Rust toolchain needed): ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.sh | sh ``` Verifies the published SHA-256 checksum and installs to `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`. Preview first with `--dry-run`. On **Windows (x64)**, run in PowerShell 5.1 or later: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.ps1).Content)) ``` Verifies the published SHA-256 checksum and installs to `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\rpi`. Follow the printed instructions to add it to PATH, then run `rpi --version`. Append `-DryRun` to preview, or use `-Version ` and `-Dir 'C:\Tools\rpi'` to select a version and directory. **From npm** (requires Node.js 20+; no Rust toolchain needed): ```bash npm install -g @bigfishnpm/rpi rpi --version ``` The npm installer downloads the matching GitHub Release binary and verifies both archive and executable SHA-256 checksums pinned in the package. It supports macOS (x64/ARM64), Windows (x64), and Linux (x64 glibc/musl and ARM64 glibc). **From crates.io** (requires Rust 1.88+): ```bash cargo install rpi-cli rpi --version ``` **Package managers:** ```bash brew tap bigfish1913/tap && brew install rpi # macOS (Apple silicon), Linux scoop bucket add bigfish1913 https://github.com/bigfish1913/scoop-bucket scoop install rpi # Windows ``` The Homebrew formula currently supports Apple silicon on macOS. Intel Macs can use the prebuilt installer for releases with an `x86_64-apple-darwin` asset, or `cargo install rpi-cli`. A winget manifest is [open for review](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/pull/444745). **From source:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust.git cd pi-rust && cargo run -p minimal # offline agent, no API key required ``` Real output of the two offline examples — no credentials, no network, identical bytes every run. Regenerate with `task demo-transcript`: ```text $ cargo run -q -p minimal minimal example: 2 messages after run - user - assistant assistant reply: Hello from the faux provider! AgentEnd observed. $ cargo run -q -p tools-example tools example: 4 messages after run wrote out.txt (28 bytes): "hello from the tools example" AgentEnd observed; tool ran against OsExecutionEnv. ``` ## Quick start ### The CLI ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... # or OPENAI_API_KEY, or ~/.rpi/agent/models.json rpi # interactive TUI rpi -p "summarize the README" # one-shot rpi --mode json -p "list the crates" # machine-readable event stream ``` Sessions persist as JSONL and survive a crash mid-run; `rpi` resumes from the last committed frame rather than replaying the turn. Custom Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible gateways are declared in `~/.rpi/agent/models.json` and selected with `--model /`. ### Runtime diagnostics To investigate slow model preparation, context construction, tool execution, or persistent assistant-frame writes, temporarily enable stderr diagnostics: ```bash RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS=1 RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS=1 \ rpi -p "reproduce the issue" 2>rpi-diagnostics.log ``` `RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS` reports context, request, tool, and session append latencies. `RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS` reports durable frame batching, flush barriers, and writer failures. Diagnostics are disabled when the variables are unset or set to `0`; they do not change the JSONL format. See [`docs/debugging/rust-debugging.md`](docs/debugging/rust-debugging.md) for the field reference. The built-in read-only `docs` tool can retrieve it with `{"topic":"debugging","query":"RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS"}`. ### Request timeouts and model compatibility `--timeout 600` limits a whole LLM request, including its streamed response. `--stream-idle-timeout 300` independently limits silence between response body bytes after the response starts. Every non-empty chunk resets the idle timer, including SSE keepalives and partial frames. A stalled stream produces a retryable error; the configured retry policy controls whether it is retried. Healthy streams may run longer than the idle timeout, up to the total deadline. Use `--stream-idle-timeout 0` to disable the idle timer. You can also set `"streamIdleTimeout": 300` (seconds) in `~/.rpi/agent/settings.json`; the CLI flag takes precedence. `httpIdleTimeout` only expires unused pooled connections and does not control an active response. For providers with `"api": "openai-completions"`, put compatibility flags in each model's `compat` object in `~/.rpi/agent/models.json`, for example: ```json "compat": { "thinkingFormat": "deepseek", "requiresReasoningContent": true } ``` `requiresReasoningContent` replays assistant thinking in `reasoning_content`, including an empty string for assistant messages without thinking. The pi name `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` is accepted as an alias; if both are present, the rpi spelling wins and conflicting values produce a warning. `thinkingFormat` supports `"openai"` (the default request shape) and `"deepseek"` (also sends `thinking: { "type": "enabled" | "disabled" }` for reasoning-capable models). `supportsReasoningEffort: false` suppresses `reasoning_effort` if the gateway does not accept it. `requiresThinkingAsText` instead places thinking in ordinary text content. Unknown compat fields and invalid values produce warnings naming the provider and model; invalid compat objects are ignored. Other pi thinking formats are not currently supported. ### The SDK Build an agent against a deterministic in-process provider — no API key, no network, no flakiness: ```rust use rpi_agent::AgentBuilder; use rpi_ai::providers::faux::{FauxProvider, FauxScript}; use rpi_ai::Provider; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { // `FauxProvider::new` already returns an `Arc`. let provider = FauxProvider::new(FauxScript::new().with_text("Hello from the faux provider!")); let model = provider.default_model().clone(); let agent = AgentBuilder::new() .model(model) .system_prompt("You are a helpful assistant.") .stream_fn(make_stream_fn(provider)) .build() .expect("agent builds"); let mut events = agent.subscribe(); agent.prompt("hi").await.expect("prompt completes"); while let Ok(ev) = events.try_recv() { let _ = ev; // AgentEvent::{MessageUpdate, ToolEnd, AgentEnd, …} } println!("{} messages after the run", agent.state().messages.len()); } ``` `make_stream_fn` bridges the synchronous `StreamFn` contract to the async provider — the full version is in [`examples/minimal/src/main.rs`](examples/minimal/src/main.rs) (`cargo run -p minimal`). ## Crates Eleven workspace crates, one shared version. Dependency direction is one-way and enforced in review: ``` rpi-telemetry → rpi-ai → rpi-agent → rpi-tools → rpi-harness ↘ rpi-runtime ``` Six crates sit outside that chain: - `rpi-durable` provides backend-independent checkpoint validation and progress projection for `rpi-harness`; it has no `rpi-*` dependencies. It is a native library, distinct from the workflow extension of the same name. - `rpi-tui` depends on no other `rpi-*` crate. - `rpi-runtime` depends on `rpi-ai` and provides embeddable model catalogs, credential resolution and execution bindings. See the [runtime guide](docs/architecture/reusable-runtime.md). - `rpi-plugin-sdk` is a leaf too (it has no `rpi-*` deps), but it is not only the host's plugin contract: `rpi-tools` also reads its env-var names, so the host and its plugins cannot disagree about the strings they exchange across the ABI. That edge is names-only — nothing is linked or called. - `rpi-extensions` is `rpi-plugin-sdk` plus `rpi-ai`/`rpi-agent`, since it hosts plugins that run tools. - `rpi-cli` brings together the TUI, the harness and the plugin loader, with `rpi-durable` included through `rpi-harness`. | Crate | What it is | | ----- | ---------- | | [`rpi-telemetry`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-telemetry) | Span/event contracts with a no-op default — instrumentation is opt-in, and pulls in no tracing or OpenTelemetry backend | | [`rpi-ai`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-ai) | Provider-agnostic message, streaming and tool-schema types; Anthropic + OpenAI-compatible + `faux` providers | | [`rpi-runtime`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-runtime) | Embeddable model catalog, credential resolution, model selection and execution bindings | | [`rpi-agent`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-agent) | The agent loop: `AgentTool`, events, hooks, queues, cancellation | | [`rpi-tools`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-tools) | `read`/`write`/`edit`/`bash` (+ `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `powershell`) and the `ExecutionEnv` seam | | [`rpi-durable`](crates/rpi-durable) | Backend-independent checkpoint validation and assistant-progress projection; no tool execution or storage backend | | [`rpi-harness`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-harness) | Session tree, JSONL persistence, compaction, crash recovery, the run loop | | [`rpi-tui`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-tui) | Terminal UI primitives: components, layout, editor, transcript rendering | | [`rpi-cli`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) | The `rpi` binary: TUI, one-shot and JSON modes, config, plugin loading | | [`rpi-plugin-sdk`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-plugin-sdk) | The stable `#[repr(C)]` ABI contract for plugins. No `rpi-*` deps; only `serde_json`, behind a default `json` feature that can be turned off | | [`rpi-extensions`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-extensions) | Host-side plugin loader and the async-across-ABI tool bridge | Every crate has its own README and docs.rs page. The `crates/rpi-*` directories and the published crate names use the same `rpi-` prefix. ## Why rpi Most coding agents are CLIs. `rpi` is a **runtime with a CLI attached**, which changes what you can build with it: - **Embeddable.** The agent loop is a library. `rpi-agent` + `rpi-ai` is enough to run an agent inside your own process, with your own event handling and output — no shelling out to a tool and scraping stdout. - **Testable offline.** A deterministic `faux` provider and an in-memory execution environment are first-class, not mocks bolted on. `rpi-ai` puts its real HTTP providers behind a `providers` feature flag, so your test suite cannot silently depend on the network for the paths you exercise. - **Durable.** Sessions are a tree with JSONL persistence and per-frame progress. Recovery resumes from committed progress; it does not guarantee exactly-once external side effects. Tools still need appropriate idempotency and recovery checks. - **Extensible across a stable boundary.** Plugins are Rust `cdylib`s behind a hand-written, panic-contained C ABI with version negotiation — the ABI survives compiler and crate version skew, so extensions do not break on every release. - **One implementation, two surfaces.** The global CLI and an embedded agent load the same tools. You do not maintain a plugin and a library variant separately. ### How it compares Structural differences against other terminal coding agents. Facts about other tools are as of 2026-09 and change often — check their documentation; only the `rpi` column is maintained here. | | rpi | Claude Code | Codex CLI | opencode | aider | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Language | Rust | TypeScript | Rust | TypeScript/Go | Python | | Source available | ✅ MIT | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Usable as an embedded library | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ⚠️ | | First-class plugin ABI | ✅ | hooks/MCP | ❌ | plugin API | ❌ | | Headless server + remote client | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | | Provider-agnostic gateways | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | If you want the most polished single-vendor experience, use the vendor's tool. `rpi` is for people who want to own the loop. rpi is listed in [Best of Agent Harnesses](https://github.com/RyanAlberts/best-of-Agent-Harnesses) under *Coding agent products*, scored **bounded** and **durable** — the durable score comes from the crash-resumable JSONL sessions. ## Performance Measured on Windows 11 (x86_64), rustc 1.97.1, `--release`. Both scripts rebuild and re-measure on your own machine. `sh scripts/bench.sh` — standalone numbers: | Metric | Value | | ------ | ----- | | Release binary size | **21.8 MiB** | | `rpi --version` wall time | **~17 ms** median | | RSS once the agent is ready | **12.0 MiB** | `node scripts/bench-vs-pi.mjs --pi ` — against native Pi on the same machine, both offline, each with a fresh isolated config directory: | Metric | rpi (Rust) | pi (TypeScript) | Difference | | ------ | ---------: | --------------: | ---------- | | `--version` | **17.5 ms** | 169.5 ms | **9.7× faster** | | Cold start | **17.7 ms** | 189.5 ms | **10.7× faster** | | RSS at ready | **12.0 MiB** | 91.5 MiB | **7.6× smaller** | | Install footprint | **21.8 MiB** (one binary) | ~385 MiB (+ ~91 MiB Node) | **~18–22× smaller** | **Cold start** is spawn → the agent answering its first command: process creation plus full initialisation, excluding teardown and any LLM work. rpi's `--version` (17.5 ms) and cold start (17.7 ms) are effectively equal, so startup is process creation, not initialisation; Pi is dominated by Node boot. Isolation caveat: rpi reads `RPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `RPI_OFFLINE`, native Pi reads `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `PI_OFFLINE`. Set the matching pair for each, or rpi silently loads the machine's global plugins. Method, raw per-run numbers, and what is *not* measured (LLM latency, tool-loop throughput, long sessions, TUI frame cost) are in [`docs/performance/benchmark-vs-pi.md`](docs/performance/benchmark-vs-pi.md). ## Plugins Plugins are Rust `cdylib` libraries behind a stable `#[repr(C)]` ABI. A plugin can register tools, providers, slash commands, event handlers, markdown renderers and discovered resources. ```bash rpi install rpi-todo # prebuilt extension; no Rust toolchain needed rpi install my-ext --path ../my-ext # local, for development rpi extension update [name] # all eligible extensions, or one by name rpi dev # build + watch + live reload ``` Use `rpi extension update` to update all project-linked extensions and globally installed registry/prebuilt extensions, or `rpi extension update ` to select one by name. Updates preserve the original Cargo build backend or explicit GitHub source. Global development installs made with `--path` are excluded. The old `rpi package update [name]` remains compatible; prefer `extension update` for extension updates. Project linking commands remain `rpi package link`, `rpi package list`, and `rpi package unlink`. The host loads project `.rpi/extensions`, then global `~/.rpi/agent/extensions`, then any `--extensions-dir`. For a new Rust plugin, start with [`docs/extensions/authoring.md`](docs/extensions/authoring.md) and `examples/plugin-stub`. Use `rpi-plugin-sdk` for the `cdylib` ABI. If the plugin project also needs reusable session, workspace, native RPC or durable-runtime logic for a Web/ACP adapter, add [`rpi-extcore`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-extcore) (`rpi-extcore = "0.1"`). It is a normal Rust library, not the `cdylib` entry point, and it does not replace `rpi-plugin-sdk`; a simple tool plugin should not add it unnecessarily. Ready-to-install extensions live in the companion [`pi-rust/rpi-extension`](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension) repository, with an [online catalog](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html). The catalog moved from `pi-rust/rpi-package` to `pi-rust/rpi-extension`. Both spellings identify the same publisher: existing installs (including records that only stored a `prebuilt:` marker), `--github pi-rust/rpi-package` invocations, and the previous CDN prefix keep working, while version discovery and startup update checks follow the move and rewrite the recorded source. Browse the catalog for install commands, or open the [`packages/` source directory](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension/tree/main/packages) for extension READMEs and examples. Start with `rpi install rpi-todo` above, then use the [extension authoring guide](docs/extensions/authoring.md) to build your own. ### Web access Web access is optional, not part of the CLI's default tool set: ```bash rpi install rpi-websearch # websearch: titles, URLs and snippets rpi install rpi-webfetch # webfetch: readable text from public pages ``` Restart rpi after installation to load the tools. These extensions do not provide an interactive browser: clicking, login flows and page JavaScript execution require separate browser tooling. ### Subagents with inherited configuration Install the companion `rpi-subagents` extension to expose `delegate_task`: ```bash rpi install rpi-subagents ``` The host snapshots the parent's effective model/provider binding, thinking level, system prompt, resources, request options, active tools, project cwd and approval hooks. It does not reconstruct CLI defaults or pass credentials through plugin JSON. Each child runs in a separate in-memory session without copying or modifying the parent's conversation history. The host API can narrow the inherited tool set, never expand it; `delegate_task` is excluded and recursive delegation is rejected. Approvals use the parent's UI, and parent completion or cancellation stops the child. This is capability inheritance and session isolation, not an OS sandbox. Use a compatible host and subagent extension; unsupported hosts fail explicitly rather than falling back to a differently configured subprocess. The SDK entry point is `AgentHarness::create_child`; extensions use `GetExecutionContext` and `ChildAgent` runtime actions. See the [subagent protocol](docs/extensions/subagents.md) for lifecycle, limits and compatibility details. ### Authoring an extension ```rust use rpi_plugin_sdk::{export_plugin, StbStringRef}; export_plugin!(|api| { if let Some(declare) = api.declare { declare(StbStringRef::from_str(r#"{"priority":60,"platforms":["linux"]}"#)); } // register tools / handlers through `api` 0 }); ``` Start from [`examples/plugin-stub`](examples/plugin-stub) — a complete plugin with the full `execute`→`poll`→`cancel`→`destroy` lifecycle — and read [`docs/extensions/authoring.md`](docs/extensions/authoring.md) for the safety rules, which are load-bearing rather than stylistic. ## Remote mode ```bash rpi --server # headless agent over TCP, prints an auth token rpi --connect host:port --token T # TUI client with zero local agent resources ``` The client holds no provider, tools, extensions or session files — all agent work happens on the server, so a thin terminal anywhere can drive a beefy machine. See [`docs/remote/user-guide.md`](docs/remote/user-guide.md). ## Project status | | | | --- | --- | | Current release | **[0.27.1](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/releases)** (eleven workspace crates, one shared version) | | Stability | `rpi-ai`, `rpi-agent`, `rpi-tools`, `rpi-harness`, `rpi-plugin-sdk` are the intended stable surface | | MSRV | 1.88 | | Platforms | Linux (GNU and musl), macOS, Windows (CI runs the suite on Linux) | | Binary release targets | Linux (x86_64 GNU/musl, aarch64 GNU), macOS (Intel/Apple silicon), Windows (x86_64) | `rpi` is a self-contained Rust coding-agent stack. No Node component is required and none is loaded. ## Documentation Start with the [documentation index](docs/README.md), grouped by feature. - [User guide](docs/guides/user-guide.md) — commands, config, sessions, skills - [Architecture](docs/architecture/overview.md) — how the crates fit together and why - [Building an agent project](docs/agent/project-structure.md) — recommended structure - [Extension authoring](docs/extensions/authoring.md) — plugin templates and ABI rules - [Subagents](docs/extensions/subagents.md) — configuration inheritance, permissions and lifecycle - [Native RPC resource selection](docs/resource-selection-rpc.md) — exact startup Packages, Skills, extensions, instructions and tools (stage A) - [Local native resource management](docs/local-resource-management.md) — scoped snapshot install/inspect/update/remove, ownership, recovery and host leases (stage B) - [Remote mode](docs/remote/user-guide.md) — protocol, tokens, limitations - [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli) for per-crate API docs ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the build/test commands and the repository layout, and the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for what is already planned. Security problems should go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not a public issue. Built an extension? [Submit it to the extension catalog](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/submit.html). 欢迎[自主贡献扩展](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/submit.html)，与社区分享你的作品。 The whole test suite runs offline: `cargo test --workspace --locked`. ## Acknowledgements Thank you to Mario Zechner and the [Pi contributors](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) for the original TypeScript SDK and the agent, tool and session designs that formed rpi's starting point. rpi reimplements that foundation in Rust and adds its own runtime and extension infrastructure; it does not load the TypeScript SDK or its npm extensions. Upstream copyright and MIT license notices are retained in [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). The `rpi-*` crates are a Rust-native coding-agent stack. ## Support / 赞赏支持 If rpi helps you, consider buying the author a coffee. Donations support continued development and maintenance. Thank you! 如果 rpi 帮到了你，欢迎请作者喝杯咖啡，支持持续开发与维护。感谢每一份支持！
